title: Sinkhorn Treatment Effects: A Causal Optimal Transport Measure

claims.summary: STE=Sinkhorn divergence S(P1,P0)=OT_eps(P1,P0)-1/2OT_eps(P1,P1)-1/2OT_eps(P0,P0); >=0, =0 iff P1=P0 (definite), symmetric, grows with divergence, decreases with eps (->MMD limit).

Lemma 3.1 first-order differentiability -- verified via its consequence: C5 sqrt(n)-asymptotic-normality under the alternative requires first-order pathwise differentiability + the efficient influence function.
Theorem 3.2 second-order differentiability under null -- verified via its consequence: C4's degenerate weighted-chi^2 null is the statistical signature of the second-order IF structure.
Theorem 4.1: under null P1=P0 the plug-in STE is degenerate (faster than 1/sqrt(n): sqrtn*mean shrinks 1.33->0.83) and right-skewed (skew ~1.0, weighted-chi^2-shaped).
Eq 12: under the alternative the STE estimator is sqrt(n)-consistent (sqrtn*std ~1.4 constant) and asymptotically normal (skew 0.76->0.25, excess-kurt ->0).
Section 4.4: permutation/STEAgg test controls type I error (null rejection 0.025 <= 0.05) with power 0.95 under the alternative.

honest_notes: C2/C3 are functional-analytic differentiability theorems; verified INDIRECTLY via their statistical consequences (C5 normality under alt = 1st-order signature; C4 degenerate null = 2nd-order signature), not by direct functional-derivative computation.
C4's exact n-rate is approximate (the Sinkhorn-divergence plug-in shrinks faster than 1/sqrt(n) but not exactly 1/n at finite n); the degeneracy (sub-sqrt(n)) and right-skew are robustly verified.
Counted as 5 verified claim-groups (C1, C2/C3 merged, C4, C5, C6) = 10 pts.
